documents/2026-09-26-winston-peters-spee.text:
# Winston Peters' Speech - “Ending The Waitangi Make-Work Industry”

*Saturday, 26 September 2026, 4:31 pm Speech: New Zealand First Party* — [https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2609/S00276/winston-peters-speech-ending-the-waitangi-make-work-industry.htm](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2609/S00276/winston-peters-speech-ending-the-waitangi-make-work-industry.htm)

## Full text

Rt Hon Winston Peters Tauranga Public Meeting Holy Trinity Church 2pm, Saturday 26th September

INTRODUCTION

It's great to be back in Tauranga, a city I came to in a snap election in 1984 and stayed for a quarter of a century.

That quarter century was a time of enormous progress from a sleepy maritime hideaway to the fastest growing city in New Zealand.

Back then there were metal roads over the Kaimai, and metal roads north of Katikati and no bridge across the harbour.

Over 25 years that dramatically changed to two toll free bridges, new roads to fill half the alphabet, and Tauranga had a real voice in parliament.

So it's great to be back.

I don't have to be a rocket scientist to work out that things are not as they used to be. And the bustling metropolis is no more. It’s 42 days till the next election, and only 30 days until early voting.

Those of you who have followed the campaign so far have noticed the obsession of the other parties with either spending or taxation.

None of them are addressing the real issue.

How to double the size of our economy by 2050 and ensure our children and grandchildren have a great future ahead.

New Zealand First does have a strategy to do just that, with the only credible policy to build a future fund to pay for it.

Today I can announce that we are helping Sun Air maintain its services to the Bay of Plenty, and we are going to build a new wharf at Matakana Island.

All part of our Regional Infrastructure Plan which is exclusively New Zealand First policy because we back the provinces.

And part of that plan also is the reduction of taxation of small and medium businesses. If your businesses turnover is $30

million or less then we are going to reduce your taxation from 28% down to 20%.

It will enable you to do more, employ more, sell more, market more and trade more.

New Zealand First is a nationalist party, all the rest are globalists. So in future we are going to do our utmost to add value to our products before we sell them overseas and increase the wealth and employment of New Zealanders.

We are going to deal to the cost of living crisis by breaking up the power gentailers so power prices come down and remove the monopoly privileges that supermarkets are using against both the suppliers and customers.

And we are not going to let the Aussie banks go on making more money in the small market of New Zealand than they are in real terms in the bigger market of Australia.

In short we are going to get our own Bank of New Zealand back which was providing real competition to Australia before Labour then National sold it off to the Aussies.

Labour (1987) sold the first third, and then National (1992) sold the second thirds of the BNZ, which at the time of sale had 6 out of 10 New Zealand banking customers.

The neoliberal apologists of both Labour and National have got a disgusting record of looking after New Zealand assets.

And the sooner you ensure they are no longer in control of the economy the better.

### Make New Zealand Healthy

No one can deny that we have a crisis in our health system. Daily news reports tell us about states of emergency being declared in our hospital, with our amazing nurses and doctors being stressed to the max and having to go to work even when they are sick.

We need more nurses right now because we have too many sick people.

Our problems extend way beyond acute care, and we should be very concerned.

The reality is shocking. In a nation of just over 5 million people we have one million suffering from one or more chronic illnesses.

Three hundred and fifty thousand have diabetes and we are told that there’s another one hundred thousand waiting to be diagnosed.

One hundred and ninety thousand are living with heart disease and ten thousand are dying from this annually.

Eighty-three thousand have dementia and this number is expected to rise to one hundred and seventy thousand by 2050. 500 more people develop dementia every week.

Sixty-nine thousand Kiwis are taking medication for ADHD up from forty-nine thousand just two years ago.

And here’s an absolute shocker. In supposedly ‘clean green 100% Pure New Zealand’ we have the second highest incidence of cancer in the world.

Currently we are spending thirty-three billion dollars on what is referred to as healthcare.

Ladies and gentlemen that’s thirty-three thousand million dollars and if by spending that huge sum of money our goal is to have a healthier nation, we are not even close.

That is why New Zealand First has a plan to Make New Zealand Healthy, a bold plan to help all Kiwis live longer healthier lives and reduce the financial pressure on the economy.

Put prevention back at the heart of healthcare. Prevention is the ultimate cure. It’s a lot easier to prevent than treat. If your house doesn’t catch on fire, you don’t need the fire engine.

Prevention is already part of the health systems job, but too often it remains a population slogan rather than something that changes what happens for the individual patient.

New Zealand’s own research shows that 59% of health spending is spent on treating chronic diseases like diabetes

and heart disease, the very illnesses that can largely be prevented - only 1.75% is spent on preventing them in the first place.

That’s not a health system. That is an ambulance at the bottom of the cliff, and New Zealanders are paying for the ambulance.

We want prevention reflected in planning, funding, and the consultation room. That means helping people reduce avoidable risk before chronic disease becomes an expensive, disabling illness.

It is not about dictating lifestyle choices; it is about making reasonable preventive care a normal part of healthcare.

Future policy must contain the following features.

Have a strong focus on metabolic health the key driver of chronic illness

Ensure that informed consent is a core part of quality healthcare

Recognise that consumer choice is what leads to healthier decisions

Promote nutrition from primary school to medical school

Require a full independent review of our dietary guidelines

Reduce the administrative burden and restore professional autonomy in General Practice

Ladies and gentlemen, everybody is talking about the cost of living or taxation but this is the most important policy in this election - for nothing is as important as health. Health crosses all boundaries, it is not a left versus right issue.

It is as important to our Maori and Pacific people as it is to our Asian and Caucasian people and regardless of what church they worship at. As Confucius is reported to have said “a healthy man has a thousand dreams, a sick man just one”. New Zealand First is talking about sound health policy as the way forward to end the epidemic of chronic illness that is affecting the lives and livelihoods of 20 percent of our population.

Ladies and Gentlemen, if you want to be talking about health after November the 7th please vote for it on November 7th.

### Citizenship

New Zealands immigration system must serve New Zealand and New Zealanders.

For too long, governments have relied on immigration to drive headline economic growth and cheap labour.

The result has been greater pressure on housing, infrastructure and public services, increased competition for entry-level jobs, and declining public confidence that immigration is being managed in the national interest.

Population growth must not outpace our ability to build the country.

New Zealand First will substantially reduce non-essential immigration and restore the principle that immigration is a privilege, not a right.

New Zealand is more than an economy. It is a nation with its own history, institutions and way of life.

New Zealand needs to start viewing our citizenship as most other countries around the world do - as a privilege that comes with special and unique rights and identity.

This does not take away from the ability for migrants looking to move here, contribute, and help build our country from showing total commitment and patriotism for New Zealand by becoming a citizen.

We in New Zealand First believe our citizenship is a privilege, not a right, and not just part of some bureaucratic machinery.

Waitangi Tribunal/Crown Maori Relations/Ministry of Maori Development

In 1975 the second Labour Government introduced the Treaty of Waitangi Tribunal to hear claims from 1975 and thereafter. The irony is that this happened at the same time as there was a huge Maori land march led by Whina Cooper, against the then Labour Government that was taking huge tracks of coastal land off Maori for “public utility purposes”.

And at the same time in 1975, the then Labour government changed the definition of Maori for Maori electoral role purposes.

From being half Maori or more, to being able to recite a Maori ancestor.

That last change has led to a dramatic miscalculation of how many Maori there are in this country. With the greatest dilution of entitlement to call yourself a Maori being as high as being 1 part in 512.

That is why today you hear so called experts and sociologists and Maori radicals claiming that Maori are 18 or 20 percent of the population.

And if we are doing a human analysis of needs by race, how on earth can we expect any accuracy? When the very basis of calculation is a total misnomer.

We who have Maori in our background are not 20 or 18 percent of the population or even 12 percent of the population. So why this pretense goes on is hard to understand unless the primary purpose of the pretense is the deceit.

Those of you who recall the American Civil Rights Movement will remember what the objective of that movement was. It was to enable black people to bust down the barriers to access the best white institutions. For only that access would give them equality.

In time they ended up with a President who came from their community. His name was Obama.

Contrast that with New Zealand, where a number of Maori radicals and their white fellow travellers have concocted an anthem of hate. And demand separate institutions, separate government, and a racial oversight of all decision making.

These radicals make these demands in the name of the mass majority of Maori. Although the mass majority of Maori haven’t asked for it.

And the proceeds of their demands thus far have seen them in privileged highly paid jobs with a mass cost consumed by their bureaucracy and nothing trickles down to their people.

That's the reason why the Waipareira trust has picked up hundreds of millions. Whilst their peoples housing, education, and health needs gather dust on the table of Maori aspirations. That way the Maori elite get rich and the Maori grievance industry grows larger.

New Zealand First understands implicitly the situation.

And we are utterly against it.

We know that Maori New Zealanders want safe affordable housing, quick affordable access to health services, easy access to the conveyor belt of education for their young, and first world wages.

Come to think of it, that is what everyone in New Zealand wants.

Once you strip out the self appointed elitists.

As a consequence if you look at the amount of money spent on Maori radio, Maori TV, and Maori health, every Maori could be in their own house now and be much healthier.

At the pinnacle of this unjustified demand on the taxpayer is the Treaty of Waitangi Tribunal.

Which has gone from a justifiable establishment to settle past grievances to so often today a make work scheme for imaginary grievances and now sees the foreshore and seabed of this country as the subject of hundreds of claims ironically with Maori against Maori for the same maritime territory.

And of late claims before the tribunal to contest the right of a mandated parliament to pass laws.

That is a direct semi judicial threat against the very essence of our democracy.

It all began in 1986, when a judicial finding loosely likened the Treaty of Waitangi to a partnership.

That judicial opinion is utterly false then and of the thousands of employers in New Zealand at the time, one said so, and he's talking to you now.

I said when I heard that judgement “if no one in the British Empire, including the home countries, was in partnership with Queen Victoria on the 5th of February 1840, how come Maori were the day after.

No judicial authority or academic expert has been able to answer that question ever since.

It is pretentious nonsense to argue otherwise.

And quickly shading from that misconception is the total deceit being marketed by “Treaty of Waitangi revisionists” that the Maori never ceded sovereignty.

This last claim is utterly false and it's made so that general claims against the population justifies remedial payments to the claimants.

The Treaty of Waitangi tribunal has become a make work organisation. Now hearing any and all claims that in a former time would’ve been dismissed on application as being inappropriate.

That's why New Zealand First today is announcing its plan to end the Treaty of Waitangi grievance industry and get back to all being equal citizens with equal rights in our country.

New Zealand First will table legislation within the first 100 days after the next election to immediately abolish the Waitangi Tribunal, and replace it with the Treaty of Waitangi Completion Commission.

Which will have the purpose of finalising all claims pre 2008, after which time its work will be finished.

The Treaty of Waitangi industry jobs will be replaced by real work. The days of the tribunal acting as an authority above parliament will be over.

We will put an end to activists using the Tribunal and taxpayers money as a platform to interfere with the direction and legislation of parliament.

Maori land reform and administrative improvements in the Maori Land Court will be a major priority for New Zealand First. Under New Zealand First, the Ministry of Maori Development will be directed to drive practical outcomes that accelerate development. The Ministry will ensure that Maori owned land, marine farming, forestry and other resources continue to enhance regional productivity, employment and community resilience.

We will ensure that all relevant policy issues pertaining to the implementation of existing Treaty of Waitangi settlements are addressed by a strengthened Ministry of Maori Development. Contemporary claims, modern policy differences, and post- settlement leadership will be the responsibility of the Ministry of Maori Development.

Crown Maori relations work will return to being the responsibility of the Ministry of Maori Development. As written into the law in 1991 when that department was established.

### Conclusion

Ladies and Gentlemen, governments matter.

If you look at Asia, the most successful economy used to be Burma. The government changed; and it's now called Myanmar and it's a cot case.

If you look at South America Venezuela used to be the leading economy; the government changed and now it's a cot case. And that is New Zealands future if you are not ultra careful in this election.

If you believe that first a racist and second a communist collection of MPs can be welded onto Labour and make a successful government then you're dreaming.

Chris Hipkins must wake up in beads of sweat at the prospect of what partners he’s got to work with when the election is over.

The Greens have sworn marxists in their parliamentary ranks.

The Maori party have sworn separatists in their ranks.

and the Opportunity party, which is the media's choice, has a tax policy that would make Stalin blush and would bankrupt nearly every retired couple.

This is an impossible combination going forward.

Working in the current coalition has not been easy largely because too many have never been in government before.

Having said that, the comparison of working with the other side is unimaginable.

Ladies and Gentlemen, New Zealand First stands for one country, called New Zealand, one flag, one standard of citizenship, one law for all, and one democracy where everybody is equal.

We have a vision of hope and growth for our country and to do that we need you.

If you give us the tools we will get the job done.

Party Vote New Zealand First.

And let’s put New Zealanders first.

documents/2026-10-09-nzfirst-to-ban-publ.title: NZFirst To Ban Public Sales Of Fireworks
documents/2026-10-09-nzfirst-to-ban-publ.text:
# NZFirst To Ban Public Sales Of Fireworks

*Friday, 9 October 2026, 10:13 am Press Release: New Zealand First Party* — [https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2610/S00076/nzfirst-to-ban-public-sales-of-fireworks.htm](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2610/S00076/nzfirst-to-ban-public-sales-of-fireworks.htm)

## Full text

New Zealand First will campaign on banning the public sale and use of fireworks across New Zealand.

Last year we introduced a members bill to ban fireworks which received tremendous public support. The legislation is already written and ready to go - it will be tabled in parliament within the first hundred days of the next government.

Guy Fawkes is a little less than four weeks away and New Zealand will see once again the multiple damaging effects it will have.

The taxpayer should not be spending millions on something that drastically impacts pets, causes the inevitable fires, and causes havoc for our emergency services. Enough is enough.

The abuse and misuse of fireworks has far outgrown any of the benefits.

This is not about being ‘nanny state’, this is about bringing some common-sense into what is a desperately needed conversation about the future of fireworks in our community.

Many major retailers have already stopped selling fireworks long ago, and there have been calls from across the country to put a stop to the sale of fireworks completely.

The legislation will stop the retail sale, manufacture, and importation of fireworks for public use. It will still allow approved public displays to continue.

This is a response to what is a hugely predictable and preventable costs for ACC, the huge costs of emergency service call outs, and most importantly stopping the effects reckless use of fireworks has on farm animals and family pets.

documents/2026-10-10-nz-first-to-increas.title: NZ First To Increase Working For Families, Minimum Wage
documents/2026-10-10-nz-first-to-increas.text:
# NZ First To Increase Working For Families, Minimum Wage

*Saturday, 10 October 2026, 3:33 pm Press Release: New Zealand First Party* — [https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2610/S00084/nz-first-to-increase-working-for-families-minimum-wage.htm](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2610/S00084/nz-first-to-increase-working-for-families-minimum-wage.htm)

## Full text

New Zealand First will campaign to introduce an uplift of the minimum wage every year for the next three years, as well as a substantial increase to Working for Families.

Low wage workers are finding the cost of living tough, especially those people who are working to support their families.

Times are difficult and our economy has taken a long time to start on the road of recovery.

An essential part of that recovery is ensuring that workers are looked after, that they are paid decent wages, have incentives to stay in work, and that those with families have enough to afford the basics in the household.

Every worker understands the concept of a fair day’s work, for a fair day’s pay.

We need to look after our workers and ensure that they receive a fair wage for their work.

It means more money in the pocket for workers, more ability to afford the basics for their families like rent, food, power, and fuel. It will mean more spending in the local economy and a more productive country on the way to economic recovery.

As a government we cannot just view the economic recovery from a national level, it needs to start with our workers who are the backbone of our communities.

### Increase to Working for Families

In April this year there was a temporary boost to the in-work tax credit of $50 a week which will only be in place for one year.

New Zealand First will make that boost permanent, and increase it by an extra $70 per week, for a total in-work tax credit to $120 per week.

Parents are working hard and we need to ensure that they have enough to support their children and their families.

This policy will turn the temporary relief into a long-term pathway for hard working parents to be able to plan for their families’ future.

This policy is estimated to cost between $500-$600 million per year.

### Increase to Minimum Wage

New Zealand First has always ensured our lowest paid workers have seen a yearly increase to the minimum wage.

We are the party that has been responsible for the yearly increase in minimum wage in three separate governments – 2005, 2017, and 2023.

New Zealand First commits to increase the minimum wage by at least inflation levels in every year of the next term of government.

Workers need to have the ability to afford the basics without falling behind the rate of inflation – it’s just common sense.

documents/2026-10-11-nzfirst-to-scrap-ac.title: NZFirst To Scrap Accredited Working Visa Model
documents/2026-10-11-nzfirst-to-scrap-ac.text:
# NZFirst To Scrap Accredited Working Visa Model

*Sunday, 11 October 2026, 2:09 pm Press Release: New Zealand First Party* — [https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2610/S00087/nzfirst-to-scrap-accredited-working-visa-model.htm](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2610/S00087/nzfirst-to-scrap-accredited-working-visa-model.htm)

## Full text

New Zealand First will end the Accredited Employer Work Visa farce and replace it with a shortage-led Skilled Work Visa.

New Zealand needs skilled migrants where New Zealanders cannot reasonably fill the job. It does not need a work-visa system that has become a general recruitment channel for routine roles with little connection to a genuine skills shortage.

The policy will put New Zealand workers first, lift confidence in the immigration system, protect migrant workers from exploitation, and preserve a clear route for employers who genuinely cannot find critical skills here.

Entry will be tied to a named occupation, region, and demonstrated need, not merely to an employer obtaining accreditation.

Immigration must serve New Zealand’s economic interests, fill identifiable shortages, and complement our workforce, not become a general source of labour for ordinary jobs. Nor be used as a back door to bring in friends and family or exploit the system.

New Zealand has approximately 171,000 unemployed people and an underutilisation rate of 13.8%. There will still be genuine shortages in particular occupations and regions, but employers seeking migrant workers for routine roles should have to prove that they have made a serious effort to employ or train New Zealanders.

### New Zealand First will:

- Scrap and replace the Accredited Employer Working Visa

- Limit access to genuine shortages

- End routine retail access

- Apply a New Zealand worker safeguard

- Restore a proper wage floor

- Require real domestic recruitment

- Strengthen employer accreditation

- Target enforcement where risk is highest

- Publish meaningful transparency data

- Protect workers without rewarding bad sponsors

If a New Zealander can reasonably be trained to do the job, then train them. If the shortage is real, prove it. If the skill is critical, New Zealand will welcome it.

But if the job is routine, the evidence is fiction, and the so-called shortage can be solved by offering a proper wage, the answer will be no.

We are a country with an immigration system, not an international labour-hire agency with a flag.

New Zealanders must come first. End of story.

documents/2026-10-13-statement-on-the-de.title: Statement On The Decision By The Minister Of Consumer Affairs Regarding Imported Aluminium Extrusions
documents/2026-10-13-statement-on-the-de.text:
# Statement On The Decision By The Minister Of Consumer Affairs Regarding Imported Aluminium Extrusions

*Tuesday, 13 October 2026, 1:17 pm Press Release: New Zealand First Party* — [https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2610/S00110/statement-on-the-decision-by-the-minister-of-consumer-affairs-regarding-imported-aluminium-extrusions.htm](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2610/S00110/statement-on-the-decision-by-the-minister-of-consumer-affairs-regarding-imported-aluminium-extrusions.htm)

## Full text

The decision today by the Minister of Consumer Affairs to decline to impose a safeguard measure on imported aluminium extrusions flooding the market is a serious backward step.

We are in the election restraint period and no decisions such as this should even be contemplated until after the election.

The decision leaves NZ companies using aluminium extrusions with no trade remedy against many inferior products being imported and those imports being sharply on the rise.

Tiwai Point makes the finest aluminium in the world, and there is no reason for New Zealand to allow the importation of inferior product, particularly when health and safety issues are involved.

The aluminium industry in New Zealand is being seriously damaged - imports are up 34% just this year alone and much of it due to the lack of safeguards of the quality of the product being imported.

While other countries have acted to ensure a fair market for their products like the US Canada, UK, European Union, and Australia - New Zealand has taken the opposite action.

Thousands of New Zealand jobs are at stake in Hamilton, New Plymouth and Wellington.

The supply chain to local fabricators and such is being threatened - as is our sovereign capability.

New Zealand has nine aluminium extrusion pressers serving the country and all of them are now at risk.

documents/2026-10-14-nzfirst-policy-anno.title: NZFirst Policy Announcement: Changes To Fast-Track Residential Approvals
documents/2026-10-14-nzfirst-policy-anno.text:
# NZFirst Policy Announcement: Changes To Fast-Track Residential Approvals

*Wednesday, 14 October 2026, 8:53 am Press Release: New Zealand First Party* — [https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2610/S00112/nzfirst-policy-announcement-changes-to-fast-track-residential-approvals.htm](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2610/S00112/nzfirst-policy-announcement-changes-to-fast-track-residential-approvals.htm)

## Full text

New Zealand First will ensure any future fast-tracked housing developments are supported by the necessary infrastructure before approval is granted.

The policy will bring a suite of changes to the current fast-track regime to ensure housing developments do not create more problems than they solve.

More housing is needed but fast-track housing developments must work in with their communities first and foremost. New Zealand First will ensure that before approvals are granted for housing projects, there will be the necessary roads, pipes, water, wastewater and other essential services approvals first.

New Zealand First backs growth, backs housing, and absolutely backs getting things built. But when we brought the blueprint for fast-track to the government three years ago, we did not envisage New Zealanders picking up the tab or suffering through developments being approved without adequate infrastructure in place.

The cart is being put before the horse, and we will ensure that ends.

New Zealand First will require fast-track housing developers to detail what infrastructure they need and demonstrate whether that infrastructure exists, is funded, and can be delivered when needed. Local authorities will also be required to provide advice on network capacity and delivery risks.

The changes would also create dedicated expert panels for housing, and give them the power to decline projects if they are not satisfied the required infrastructure will be in place.

There would be a sunset period for those already listed housing projects currently enjoying preferential access to fast-track.

A listing for fast-track should not be a perpetual entitlement. If a listed project has not lodged its application by the end of 2028, it will lose its preferential access. That means any eventual application must be reassessed against contemporary infrastructure and planning realities through a referral application.

The reforms will also streamline decision-making by making the Minister for Housing responsible for housing project referral decisions.

People don’t live in a world where critical infrastructure is an afterthought. They live in communities that rely on reliable roads, water, wastewater systems and transport links.

We want a system that is faster, smarter and more practical. If we are serious about housing for New Zealanders, then we must be equally serious about the pipes, roads and services that make those developments viable.

documents/2026-10-15-nz-first-announces-.title: NZ First Announces Overhaul To Regulate Combat Sports
documents/2026-10-15-nz-first-announces-.text:
# NZ First Announces Overhaul To Regulate Combat Sports

*Thursday, 15 October 2026, 1:35 pm Press Release: New Zealand First Party* — [https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2610/S00133/nz-first-announces-overhaul-to-regulate-combat-sports.htm](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2610/S00133/nz-first-announces-overhaul-to-regulate-combat-sports.htm)

## Full text

New Zealand First will back Combat Sports and establish a statutory Combat Sports Commission to enforce participant safety, eliminate unsanctioned events, and block criminal influence.

The lack of modern regulation creates severe risks for athletes and undermines legitimate clubs.

Following coronial recommendations after the tragic death of Kain Parsons, alongside growing concerns over gang-affiliated bare-knuckle fights and unsanctioned prize-money events, New Zealand First will deliver decisive reform.

### New Zealand First will:

- Establish a Combat Sports Commission to oversee nationwide event licensing and contestant registration.

- Introduce minimum health and medical standards, such as pre- and post-fight medical examinations, serological clearances, attending medical practitioners at all events, and mandatory stand-down period between contests determined by medical professionals.

- Empower the Commission to focus on licensing events and promoters.

- Introduce a penalty regime for illegal and unsanctioned events.

- Formalise recognition and partnership with Sport New Zealand to support legitimate promoters and athletes.

This comprehensive reform ensures safer ringsides, clean competition, and public confidence across New Zealand’s combat sports sector.

Notes:

### Commitments:

- We will recognise Combat Sports as a key physical activity and sport in New Zealand by supporting a partnership investment with Sports NZ.

- Combat sports has grown significantly over the past two decades, particularly MMA, kickboxing, Muay Thai and Brazilian Jiu Jitsu, and traditional boxing and wrestling. Social Media, massive promotions like the UFC, and New Zealand’s own success in Combat Sports has seen many New Zealanders look to combat sports and martial arts as their activity of choice.

- New Zealand has punched above its weight internationally in combat sports producing many amateur and professional world champions across boxing, grappling, wrestling, kick boxing, the Asian martial arts, and Mixed Martial Arts.

- Well known champions include David Tua (Boxing), Joseph Parker (Boxing), Carlos Ulberg (Recent UFC champion), Israel Adesanya (Former UFC champion), Mea Motu (Boxing) and many others.

- NZ First also wants to change the conversation about health - we want to Make New Zealand Healthy. Too much of the conversation is about managing sickness and not enough about prevention. Sport and physical exercise has always had its place in a sporting nation like ours, but we also have an obesity epidemic with the increase in sedentary lifestyles.

- In today’s society we are facing mental health challenges especially affecting our young. We’re a warrior nation and we need to instil a warrior ethos for our young. The Martial Arts aren’t just physical exercise but also provide psychosocial benefits such as confidence, resilience, interpersonal skills, comradery, and discipline.

- We also see a lot of New Zealanders slip through the cracks and look to combat sports to turn a new leaf. Many trainers, including the ones in this room, have specialised and targeted youth programs which help keep young people off the streets.

- Other major sports such as Netball NZ will receive $920,000pa, NZMMAF has not received any funding from Sports NZ despite its mainstream participation from young and old alike.

- As part of the next Government, New Zealand First will improve recognition of all Combat Sports and Martial Arts National Sport Organisations and review rules around investment partner status with Sports NZ

- We will establish a Combat Sports Commission to ensure fighter safety and integrity across amateur and professional competition.

- Why do we need a Combat Sports Commission?

- Tens of thousands of New Zealanders participate in combat sports and thousands compete in both amateur and professional competitions.

- Legislation is decades out of date and combat sports has changed drastically over that time. Modern MMA, Boxing, and Kickboxing hadn’t existed in their current commercial forms and thanks to New Zealanders’ warrior ethos many Kiwis participate regularly across combat sports and martial arts.

- New Zealand also lags internationally, we have a largely unregulated combat sports and martial arts market compared to Australia, UK, and the US. A Combat Sports Commission will consider the modern environment and most importantly improve competition safety standards and protect fighters.

- There have been avoidable deaths due to lack of reporting and medical standards and we cannot risk that of any New Zealander. As more New Zealanders participate, with more trainers, and event promoters as a result, we need to ensure minimum health and medical standards are developed and followed.

- There is also the benefit of attracting international fight events to New Zealand. We have had a UFC event here, but despite having multiple fighters and champions we haven’t been able to secure more events.

- What will the Combat Sports Commission do?

- We have already drafted a Member’s Bill that sets out details but , but more work needs to be done in order to get this off the ground. What’s important is that a commitment to take action has been made.

- This means that combat sport competitions have to be licensed, and that organisers have to work to a mandatory set of safety standards to ensure fighter safety.

- Those standards included pre and post fight medical examinations, medical suspensions, and mandatory attendance of medical practitioners at events.

- We will outlaw unlicensed competition, and introduce a penalty regime to improve accountability in the sport.

- Oversight will move from Police, who under the Boxing and Wrestling Act 1981 provided licenses for events, to the Commission, who I expect would have experts in the Combat Sports Industry.

- This is about safety in a growing, popular, contact sport. All of the trainers here are veterans of combat sports and they are calling for this. Inaction will mean that someone will get seriously hurt or killed.

- How will the Combat Sports Commission be funded?

- The final form and structure is still to be decided and we need collaboration across all of Combat Sports so that we produce something workable.

- What we don’t want to do is establish a massive piece of bureaucracy that ends up making life too hard for many trainers and competitors who do this for a passion. However a structure that improves accountability, expertise, and has the right people in place would be a big step in the right direction.

### BACKGROUND

- Combat sports have grown significantly in New Zealand over the past two decades, particularly MMA, kickboxing, Muay Thai and Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu, alongside traditional boxing and wrestling. New Zealand athletes have achieved success on the international stage, contributing to increased participation and commercial interest in the sector.

- The principal legislation governing combat sport contests remains the Boxing and Wrestling Act 1981, was enacted more than 40 years ago and has since been repealed. The Act regulated boxing and wrestling contests but does not adequately cover the ‘Asian Martial Arts’ or modern combat sports such as MMA and kickboxing. We need a fit for purpose piece of legislation.

- As a result, many combat sports operate under a mixture of voluntary codes, private promoters and sporting organisations, with no consistent national framework governing all combat sports.

- Increased commercialisation, online promotion, prize money competitions and spectator interest have heightened concerns regarding participant safety, event oversight and public confidence in the sector.

### PROBLEMS TO ADDRESS

- New Zealand's regulatory framework has not kept pace with the emergence and growth of modern combat sports, leaving significant gaps in oversight and enforcement.

- There is currently no consistent nationwide system governing fighter registration, event licensing, medical requirements or participant safety standards across all combat sports.

- Combat sports carry a heightened risk of concussion, head trauma and other serious injuries. Though many practitioners, coaches, and promoters ensure the necessary safety equipment, there is no minimum standard across all different codes.

- The death of Kain Parsons following a charity boxing match prompted coronial recommendations for stronger participant education, concussion management and event safeguards.

- Recent reporting has highlighted the emergence of unsanctioned combat events operating outside recognised sporting structures, raising concerns regarding participant welfare, legal liability and public safety.

- There have also been concerns about gang-affiliated fighting events and the potential for organised crime to exploit combat sports competitions, creating law and order risks alongside athlete welfare concerns.

- These issues risk undermining legitimate combat sports clubs and promoters that operate safely and professionally.

### POLICY SOLUTIONS

- Establish a statutory Combat Sports Commission as a Crown entity responsible for regulating combat sports nationwide.

- Require organisers to obtain a contest licence before promoting or conducting a combat sports contest. Unlicensed events would be subject to fines of up to $10,000 for individuals and $20,000 for organisations.

- Require all contestants to be formally registered before participating in regulated combat sports contests.

- Give the Commission authority to refuse licences where events or promoters have direct or indirect gang associations, or where Police advise there are significant public safety risks.

- Introduce mandatory medical safeguards including:

- Pre-fight medical examinations.

- Post-fight medical examinations.

- Current serological clearances.

- Mandatory attendance of medical practitioners at events.

- A mandatory medical stand-down period between contests.

- Allow the Commission to create sport-specific rules and safety standards for different combat disciplines.

- Formalise engagement with Sport New Zealand and improve recognition of legitimate combat sports organisations within the wider sports sector.

documents/2026-10-15-nz-first-to-increas.title: NZ First To Increase Funding And Support To NZ Coastguard
documents/2026-10-15-nz-first-to-increas.text:
# NZ First To Increase Funding And Support To NZ Coastguard

*Thursday, 15 October 2026, 1:51 pm Press Release: New Zealand First Party* — [https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2610/S00135/nz-first-to-increase-funding-and-support-to-nz-coastguard.htm](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2610/S00135/nz-first-to-increase-funding-and-support-to-nz-coastguard.htm)

## Full text

New Zealand First will increase government funding of NZ Coastguard, ensuring this vital frontline service has the resources it needs to continue protecting New Zealanders on the water.

Coastguard’s annual budget (NZ$30–34m) is roughly 40% funded by the New Zealand Government and 60% by public support.

Under New Zealand First, Crown funding will increase to 70% of Coastguard's operating costs - an increase of $12 million a year.

This investment will provide greater funding certainty and ensure Coastguard can meet growing demand while maintaining the high standards of service New Zealanders rely on.

Coastguard is New Zealand's primary maritime search and rescue organisation. It has more than 2,000 volunteers operating from 62 units nationwide, Coastguard responds to emergencies across our coastlines, harbours, rivers and lakes, bringing thousands of New Zealanders safely home every year.

In the 2024/25 year alone, Coastguard responded to 2,785 incidents, assisted 6,792 people and saved 61 lives.

The additional funding will support critical maintenance and capability investment, including upgrades to New Zealand's VHF maritime communications network, vessel procurement and replacement, and the purchase of essential rescue equipment.

It will also strengthen Coastguard's volunteer workforce through improved training, capability development, and practical support measures such as subsidising volunteer travel costs.

In addition, New Zealand First will also improve coordination between Coastguard New Zealand, New Zealand Police, New Zealand Search and Rescue, Fire and Emergency New Zealand, Health New Zealand and the New Zealand Defence Force. Better cooperation between agencies will improve capital procurement, strengthen interoperability, reduce duplication, and ensure emergency services can respond more effectively when lives are at risk.

Coastguard volunteers give their time freely to keep New Zealanders safe.

New Zealand First believes the Government must ensure this essential national service has the funding, equipment, and support it needs to continue saving lives of New Zealanders.

1. NZFirst will review Coastguard’s funding arrangement to lift baseline funding and establish a contracting model that will ensure they receive:

a. Adequate access to capital for critical maintenance and capability investment,

b. Improved workforce capability, and

c. volunteer support for training, wear and tear, and call out support

2. NZFirst will also review arrangements across Land Search and Rescue New Zealand, Surf Life Saving NZ, and St Johns to ensure that their volunteers are adequately supported.

3. NZFirst will investigate the establishment of an ‘Emergency Response Capital Grants Fund’ so that charitable organisations involved in emergency response have a secure funding option when making decisions about replacing equipment.

4. NZFirst will conduct a review of emergency management services - Coastguard, NZ Police, NZSAR, Fire and Emergency NZ, Health NZ, Civil Defence and the NZ Defence Force to improve response coordination and interoperability between services.

documents/2026-10-16-nz-first-will-immed.title: NZ First Will Immediately Reverse This Week’s Decision By The Minister Of Consumer Affairs
documents/2026-10-16-nz-first-will-immed.text:
# NZ First Will Immediately Reverse This Week’s Decision By The Minister Of Consumer Affairs

*Friday, 16 October 2026, 1:13 pm Press Release: New Zealand First Party* — [https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2610/S00145/nz-first-will-immediately-reverse-this-weeks-decision-by-the-minister-of-consumer-affairs.htm](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2610/S00145/nz-first-will-immediately-reverse-this-weeks-decision-by-the-minister-of-consumer-affairs.htm)

## Full text

NZFirst will immediately reverse this week’s decision by the Minister of Consumer Affairs before the end of this year.

Today we have visited Vulcan Aluminium in Hamilton to discuss the recent announcement by the Minister of Consumer Affairs to not impose a safeguard measure on imported aluminium extrusions flooding the market.

Thousands of New Zealand jobs are at stake.

The decision to not impose safeguards leaves NZ companies using aluminium extrusions with no trade remedy against many inferior products flooding the market.

The supply chain to local fabricators and wider industry is being threatened - as is our sovereign capability.

New Zealand has nine aluminium extrusion pressers serving the country and all of them are now at risk.

Australia, UK, US, EU, and Canada have all taken action and so should we.

We are a nationalist party who puts New Zealand and New Zealanders first.

documents/2026-10-18-nzfirst-campaign-an.title: NZFirst Campaign Announcement: Commuter Rail For Christchurch, Reinstate Southerner Train
documents/2026-10-18-nzfirst-campaign-an.text:
# NZFirst Campaign Announcement: Commuter Rail For Christchurch, Reinstate Southerner Train

*Sunday, 18 October 2026, 2:29 pm Press Release: New Zealand First Party* — [https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2610/S00155/nzfirst-campaign-announcement-commuter-rail-for-christchurch-reinstate-southerner-train.htm](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2610/S00155/nzfirst-campaign-announcement-commuter-rail-for-christchurch-reinstate-southerner-train.htm)

## Full text

New Zealand First is announcing today that we will be committing to a 12-month trial of commuter rail in Canterbury - from Rolleston to Christchurch and from Rangiora to Christchurch.

We will also commit to bringing back the Southerner Train that connected Christchurch with Dunedin and Invercargill.

We will work with the current operators of the Mainlander train service on that route, to secure a commercially sound agreement that gets more trains running.

We want to see the Mainlander become a more frequent service, reconnecting the cities and towns of the South Island.

This will give Cantabrians a real alternative to sitting in traffic every morning and every evening.

Our ambition is to get passengers from Rolleston to central Christchurch in around 20 minutes by train, instead of spending up to 50 minutes on the road.

And the trains will stop near Colombo Street, bringing passengers back into the heart of Christchurch.

A permanent commuter railway can’t be built on wishful thinking. It needs passengers, it needs to make economic sense, and it needs to demonstrate that Cantabrians actually want it.

We will give Cantabrians the opportunity to prove it works in practice, not just theory.

If hundreds use these trains every day, that will build the business case for a permanent service, and hundreds a day becomes thousands. And more frequent trains then become hundreds of thousands.

That is how we make the case for new stations, better connections, and the long-term investment needed to make commuter rail a permanent feature of Canterbury.

The railway lines are already here and the taxpayer owns them. For decades, they have been passing through the communities without carrying the people who live in them. We believe that should change.

We are not proposing to spend years and millions of dollars studying whether Cantabrians might catch a train. We are proposing to put the trains on and find out.

That is the difference between talking about rail and delivering it.

New Zealand First will give Canterbury the opportunity to prove that commuter rail works.

We will put the trains on. The rest is up to Canterbury.

documents/2026-10-19-statement-on-labour.title: Statement On Labour’s Proposed Social Media Ban For Under-16s
documents/2026-10-19-statement-on-labour.text:
# Statement On Labour’s Proposed Social Media Ban For Under-16s

*Monday, 19 October 2026, 1:32 pm Press Release: New Zealand First Party* — [https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2610/S00162/statement-on-labours-proposed-social-media-ban-for-under-16s.htm](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2610/S00162/statement-on-labours-proposed-social-media-ban-for-under-16s.htm)

## Full text

19 October 2026

Labour’s announcement to ban social media for under 16-year-olds is a naive solution to a genuine issue.

Throwing out simplistic sound bites denies the reality that banning social media in its entirety means either banning VPNs or using digital ID for everyone - otherwise it’s a fool’s errand and meaningless.

The failure in Australia to implement such laws highlights this and Labour knows it.

Everyone with children wants them protected from the harms of social media, but the threat of everyone needing to lose privacy and freedoms to enable that to happen is what Labour needs to explain to kiwis.

Ultimately, we need to ask ourselves as a country how far we want the government to overreach into the responsibilities of parents, but most importantly the rights of parents.

If we start down this innocent pathway, it will become very slippery and won’t stop.

Election period promises that sound good should not hide the serious nature of the solution, nor of the seriousness of the problem we all agree should be addressed.

PS

Between 2020-2023 what did Labour ever do about the problem they are now promising to solve.

documents/2026-10-20-nzfirst-to-fund-nzs.title: NZFirst To Fund NZs Gaming Industry Sector, Keeping Talent And Companies In NZ
documents/2026-10-20-nzfirst-to-fund-nzs.text:
# NZFirst To Fund NZs Gaming Industry Sector, Keeping Talent And Companies In NZ

*Tuesday, 20 October 2026, 4:17 pm Press Release: New Zealand First Party* — [https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2610/S00174/nzfirst-to-fund-nzs-gaming-industry-sector-keeping-talent-and-companies-in-nz.htm](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2610/S00174/nzfirst-to-fund-nzs-gaming-industry-sector-keeping-talent-and-companies-in-nz.htm)

## Full text

New Zealand First is announcing today a funding commitment that will grow our Creative Industry sector, help grow our economy, and keep kiwi talent, skills and companies in New Zealand.

New Zealand First provided early support for the video gaming industry by investing $10 million from the Provincial Growth Fund into the Centre of Digital Excellence (CODE) based in Dunedin. CODE provides grants to local creators to build prototypes, establish new studios, and scale existing businesses. It also acts as an incubator, offering targeted workshops and commercial advice.

The Video Game industry is an often overlooked in the Creative Industry sector. New Zealand’s Game Development Industry has hit $1 billion in annual revenue this year, a growth of 33.5% on the 2025 figures.

The Global Video Game industry at US$184 billion dwarfs both the US$33.9 billion Global Box Office and US$28.6 billion Global Music industries combined.

Video Games are now the largest entertainment industry in the world and New Zealand has an opportunity to massively benefit economically from that industry.

CODE has seen the establishment of 20 new studios, with one becoming so successful that its corporation tax paid in the last few years has paid for CODE’s original provincial 6-year grant programme.

This is sustainable economic development, not a government hand-out.

The Gaming Development Sector Rebate (GDSR) is currently at $40 million per year and allows studios to grow and compete on the world stage, but we are currently limiting its use and we intend to remove that limitation so they can grow, build faster, and employ and retain our people in New Zealand.

In 2026 the rebate paid out $21.9 million to local studios and returned $213 million in income tax and PAYE. The return to the Government is $9.73 for every dollar invested.

The issue is that the Gaming Sector has room to grow but because of limited settings of the Rebate our CODE supported local talent is being poached by Australia. Even though the industry has enjoyed massive growth over the last 5 years we risk stunting our industry’s growth.

New Zealand First aims to double our economy by 2050 and in order to do so we have to support successful domestic industries to reach that target.

That is why we are announcing today that we will:

### 1. Improve the Gaming Development Sector Rebate scheme. We will:

a. Increase the GDSR that studios can receive from 20% to 40% to support accelerated growth to $3billion in export revenue by 2030 and much higher than that by 2050.

b. Increase the amount Gaming Studios can claim from $3 million to $10 million. This will allow our largest studios to continue to grow jobs in New Zealand and keep our sector graduates onshore.

c. Increase the annual appropriation of the Gaming Development Sector Rebate from $40 million to $45 million by 2028 to further support the growth of the sector.

d. Lower the threshold that Gaming Studios can start claiming from $250,000 to $150,000 to allow smaller studios to start developing earlier.

In order to secure the future development of local creators we are also committing to:

### 2. Funding certainty for the Centre of Digital Excellence (CODE)

a. We will provide funding certainty for CODE by baselining its current budget of $5m per annum to ensure that the Gaming sector has certainty year on year.

b. We will also commit to expanding its budget to $7m by 2028 to ensure that we have the talent needed for a growing Video Game Sector.

CODE secures the future pipeline of studios and skilled workers for the industry, and some will grow, with the support of the GDSR programme, into the big, successful studios of the future to accelerate our industry from a billion to three billion dollars of revenue by 2030.

New Zealand First is the only party that is encouraging and planning for the growth of our economy.

documents/2026-10-22-nzfirst-law-and-ord.title: NZFirst Law And Order Policy Announcement: Tougher Sentences, Degrees Of Murder, Smashing Organised Crime
documents/2026-10-22-nzfirst-law-and-ord.text:
# NZFirst Law And Order Policy Announcement: Tougher Sentences, Degrees Of Murder, Smashing Organised Crime

*Thursday, 22 October 2026, 6:08 pm Press Release: New Zealand First Party* — [https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2610/S00200/nzfirst-law-and-order-policy-announcement-tougher-sentences-degrees-of-murder-smashing-organised-crime.htm](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2610/S00200/nzfirst-law-and-order-policy-announcement-tougher-sentences-degrees-of-murder-smashing-organised-crime.htm)

## Full text

New Zealand First is today announcing a Law-and-Order policy package that will back our law enforcement, hold offenders to account, and keep our community safe.

New Zealanders deserve to feel safe, secure, and have their person and property respected.

To build safer communities, the government must ensure that the NZ Police have the resources and tools to do their job. New Zealand First is the only party in three decades with the record of seriously boosting police numbers with the necessary funding, training, and personnel to meet the challenges of our growing population.

Our justice system and sentencing regime needs to work properly while ensuring that victims of crime are prioritised over offenders.

We believe that for the most serious crimes of first-degree murder and rape or murder of a child, life means life – with no chance of parole.

We believe organised crime, in particular the growing influence of transnational crime, needs to be dismantled and we will establish a dedicated agency to come down hard on organised criminal activity.

We believe that the judicial system in many cases has failed to ensure offenders are held to account and justice is being delivered. We will significantly increase the use of minimum mandatory sentences for serious violent and sexual offenders.

We will introduce a formal degrees of murder regime that will ensure charges of murder are appropriately categorised with a higher chance of success and not fail due to technicalities.

We will increase the thresholds of parole eligibility.

We will strengthen the Coward Punch law to ensure a minimum mandatory prison sentence of eight years non-parole for causing death.

### New Zealand First full Law and Order policy package:

### Police and Enforcement

- Ensure that police have the resources to do their job.

- Establish a dedicated agency for organized crime with a responsible minister to dismantle transnational criminal networks.

- Abolish the Serious Fraud Office (SFO) and replace it with a specialised division within the NZ Police.

### Justice

- Increase the use of mandatory minimum sentences for serious violent and sexual offenders.

- Put victims first by developing a reparation system where the state assumes responsibility for immediate reparation to victims and responsibility for recovery from the offenders.

- Increase sentences for attempted murder and wounding with intent to cause grievous bodily harm from 14 years to 25 years.

- Introduce a formal 'degrees of murder' regime that increases the minimum non-parole period from 10 to 20 years and recognises

- 1st Degree Murder which is life imprisonment without parole - “Life means life”.

- 2nd Degree Murder which is aggravated life sentence with a minimum sentence non-parole period of 30 years

- 3rd Degree Murder which is pre-meditated life sentence with a minimum non-parole period of 10 years

- Limit sentence discounts for factors other than a guilty plea to 10%. Guilty plea discounts will remain limited to 25% to ensure clearer demarcations.

- Raise standard parole eligibility to 75% of a sentence for long-term offenders. Those convicted of murder must be assessed as having a low probability of reoffending before release

- New Zealand First will strengthen the ‘Coward Punch’ law so that Coward punches causing death, will require Judges to impose a minimum non-parole period of 8 years imprisonment.

- Review transport penalty regimes to achieve greater consistency (e.g., comparing red-light running with stop-sign running), effectiveness (fines versus demerits), and efficacy (infringements versus court-required appearances)

- Oppose any further extension of the Clean-Slate law.

- Require District Courts to proactively publish sentencing notes within 72 hours and limit final name suppression to extreme cases. This aims to ensure openness prevails in the legal system.

- Treat burglary to a home or private dwelling the same as aggravated burglary or home invasion, recognising that this type of crime has impacts against the person not just property.

- Strengthen self-defence laws by:

- Investigating the implementation of ‘Castle Doctrine’ and ‘Stand Your Ground’ laws so that individuals have the confidence to defend their person and their property without a duty to retreat.

- Amend Police operational and prosecution guidelines to make it clear that a person who “excessively defends” themselves or another when attacked or confronted in their own home or business is to be treated as a victim unless overwhelming evidence to the contrary is collected.

- Amend the Solicitor-General’s prosecution guidelines to ensure substantial weight is given to the unlikelihood of a New Zealand jury finding guilty, a person who “excessively defends” themselves or another when attacked or confronted in their own home or business.

- Require the Solicitor-General to review and endorse any intention to prosecute a person defending themselves or another when confronted in their own business or home, including declaring the prosecution is in the public interest and considered likely to result in a conviction.

- NZ First will defend our children and introduce tougher penalties for sexual violation, including life imprisonment for rape against children.

documents/2026-10-23-nzfirst-policy-anno.title: NZFirst Policy Announcement: 50% Targeted Accelerated Depreciation For Manufacturing And Export Sector
documents/2026-10-23-nzfirst-policy-anno.text:
# NZFirst Policy Announcement: 50% Targeted Accelerated Depreciation For Manufacturing And Export Sector

*Friday, 23 October 2026, 3:43 pm Press Release: New Zealand First Party* — [https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2610/S00209/nzfirst-policy-announcement-50-targeted-accelerated-depreciation-for-manufacturing-and-export-sector.htm](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2610/S00209/nzfirst-policy-announcement-50-targeted-accelerated-depreciation-for-manufacturing-and-export-sector.htm)

## Full text

New Zealand’s weak productivity growth and insufficient business investment remain longstanding economic challenges. Businesses need modern machinery, technology and equipment to increase output, reduce costs, and compete internationally.

New Zealand First is the only party committed to doubling the New Zealand Economy by 2050, and in order to do that we must have policies focused on lifting productivity and gross domestic product.

The Government introduced Investment Boost in Budget 2025, allowing businesses to deduct 20% of the cost of eligible new investment assets upfront, followed by normal depreciation on the remaining 80%. The scheme applies to qualifying assets acquired or brought into use from 22 May 2025.

The current scheme is a depreciation uplift across all depreciable property. New Zealand First is supportive of targeted new plant, machinery, and equipment with high productivity returns.

Industrial machinery and equipment require substantial upfront capital over long timeframes. This means that large upfront capital outlay is required before equipment is operational and that such equipment typically has long payback periods.

International evidence clearly demonstrates that front-loaded depreciation for machinery and equipment accelerates capital investment, lifts productivity, and delivers measurable increases in GDP. Like-minded economies already have such policies in play and we need to ensure that our economy is competitive.

- NZ First will lift productivity by introducing a targeted accelerated depreciation rate of 50% in the first year for new plant, machinery and equipment for the manufacturing sector and targeted export sectors.

- The policy is not an expansion to the existing Investment Boost, but increases the first year depreciation rate only on new plant, machinery, and equipment, and only for businesses in the manufacturing and targeted export sectors such as primary production - mining, aquaculture, forestry, farming, and fishing.

New Zealand First backs our manufacturing sector and value-added export sectors and this policy is targeted to those sectors. Manufacturers across New Zealand and Primary industry production such as farming, fishing, aquaculture, horticulture, and mining will benefit from this policy.

This targeted expansion to investment boost complements other New Zealand First economic policies such as reducing the Company tax rate for SMEs from 28% to 20%, the establishment of a Temasek-model $100 billion New Zealand Future Fund, driving the cost of energy down by splitting the gentailers, target tax incentives for international investment into nationally significant infrastructure, incentivising value added dairy manufacturing, establishing a Special Economic Zone at Marsden Point, returning 50% of mining royalties back to their regions, and backing a New Zealand Owned Bank capable of competing with foreign owned banks.

```text
Accessibility Standards Bill
Member’s Bill
Explanatory note
General policy statement
The Accessibility Standards Bill is needed to ensure that all New Zealanders can
access public and essential services that underpin daily life, including education,
transport, telecommunications, justice, banking, essential household utilities, and ser‐
vices provided by Crown organisations and local authorities.
The 2023 Census identified that 17 percent of people living in New Zealand house‐
holds were disabled, including 98,000 children and more than 750,000 adults. Disa‐
bility prevalence increases significantly with age, affecting more than a third of
people aged 65 and over. The numbers of persons with disabilities and access needs
are set to rise in an ageing population.
Accessibility means people can live independently and participate fully in all parts of
life with dignity, agency, and choice. This is a challenge that affects a wide range of
people, including seniors, families, workers recovering from injury, returned service‐
men and women, and communities across regional New Zealand. Independent
research confirms that New Zealand’s accessibility system is fragmented, reactive,
and lacking clear accountability, with non‑mandatory standards that are not consis‐
tently embedded in practice. The cost of inaccessibility falls on seniors, disabled
people and their families, including reduced economic and social participation, lost
income, increased stress, and higher health costs. Over time, these private burdens
compound into public costs: higher health expenditure, social disruption, and lost pro‐
ductivity.
International experience demonstrates that a different approach is possible. Jurisdic‐
tions such as Australia show that when accessibility standards are enabled in primary
legislation, systems shift from being reactive to preventative. Infrastructure progres‐
sively becomes more usable across its lifespan, complaints decrease, and economic
participation increases. Binding standards provide clarity for government, businesses
and service providers, reducing uncertainty and duplication while improving out‐
DRAFT FOR CONSULTATION
```

```text
This Bill seeks to address this issue by providing for the development and approval of
practical accessibility standards, establishing a streamlined complaints process for
contraventions of those standards, and promoting advice, education, and training in
relation to accessibility issues and accessibility standards. The framework is designed
to balance the need for reasonable accommodation with the need to avoid imposing
unjustifiable costs on affected entities. Embedding accessibility in law supports fiscal
responsibility, prepares New Zealand for demographic change, strengthens regional
and disaster resilience, and reinforces the integrity of public services and the justice
system. The Bill provides a practical and proportionate mechanism to ensure that
New Zealand’s infrastructure and services are accessible and usable for everyone.
```

### Page 1

```text
Container Return Scheme Bill
Member’s Bill
Explanatory note
General policy statement
New Zealand consumers produce more than two billion beverage containers as waste
every year. Many of these end up in landfills, stockpiles, rivers, and on beaches rather
than being recycled. For years, councils and ratepayers have carried the cost of clean‐
ing up this waste while the producers of beverage containers largely avoid responsi‐
bility.
A practical solution already exists. Container return schemes operate successfully
across Australia, Europe, North America, and elsewhere. These schemes place a
small refundable deposit on beverage containers which consumers receive back when
the container is returned for recycling. Overseas evidence shows that such schemes
can dramatically reduce litter and significantly increase recycling rates.
New Zealand has already undertaken extensive work to design a container return
scheme. Between 2019 and 2022, central government, local councils, industry repre‐
sentatives, and community groups participated in a detailed co-design process to
develop a model suitable for New Zealand. Following that work, Cabinet considered
implementing a national scheme. However, in March 2023, the Government decided
to defer the rollout of the scheme despite the substantial design work already having
been completed.
This Bill finishes the job. The purpose of this Bill is to establish the legislative frame‐
work for a national container return scheme and require the Government to imple‐
ment it. The Bill sets out the core principles of the scheme while leaving operational
detail to regulations, allowing the final design to be refined using the extensive policy
work that has already been undertaken.
Clause by clause analysis
Clause 1 is the Title clause.
```

## Full text

### Page 1

```text
Financial Markets Conduct (Preventing Payment Scams)
Amendment Bill
Member’s Bill
Explanatory note
General policy statement
This Bill would make New Zealand’s financial system a safer place for consumers by
addressing payment scams. Even though the New Zealand Banking Association Code
of Banking Practice includes five commitments intended to reduce fraudulent transac‐
tions — like pre-transaction warnings, check of payee systems, and improved report‐
ing on scams — these are all focused on the responsibilities of a sending bank and do
not apply to receiving banks or financial service providers.
Receiving banks, who can receive stolen funds, and who may inadvertently play a
central role in money laundering operations, are not currently required to filter incom‐
ing payments for suspicious activity. Such a limitation significantly diminishes the
efficacy of scam prevention.
Financial service providers handling large sums of money on behalf of consumers are
not verified by banks as legitimately able to carry out such transactions, leaving
impersonators able to carry out fraudulent transactions undetected.
To address these shortcomings, the Bill proposes amending the Financial Markets
Conduct Act 2013 to introduce a duty to protect consumers from payment scams.
This change meets the aims of the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing
of Terrorism Act 2009, combatting organised crime, and is founded on international
best practice. By making receiving banks as accountable as sending banks for identi‐
fying and combating fraud, and extending duties of care for financial service provid‐
ers, the Bill intends to provide a better and more equitable system for keeping New
Zealanders safe from payment scams.
Equally, all institutions involved in reducing financial fraud will be held accountable
for timeliness response to alerts.
```

```text
446JA Duty to protect consumers from payment scams
(1) Every financial institution must take all reasonable steps to protect consumers
from payment scams.
(2) The requirement to protect consumers includes all of the following:
(a) ensuring a confirmation of payee system is operational:
(b) ensuring an identity verification process that meets the requirements of
the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act
2009 is operational:
(c) educating consumers about the risk of payment scams:
(d) ensuring staff have the requisite knowledge, expertise, and training to
identify and warn consumers about the risk of payment scams:
(e) identifying vulnerable consumers and taking appropriate precautions to
mitigate those consumers’ heightened vulnerability to payment scams:
(f) providing advice and assistance to consumers who believe they have
been subject to a payment scam, including ensuring that such advice and
assistance is easily accessible at any time of day:
(g) implementing and continually improving systems that align with inter‐
national best practice standards to detect and warn consumers where
there is evidence of particular payment scams occurring within New
Zealand:
```

```text
Fireworks Prohibition Legislation Bill
Member’s Bill
Explanatory note
General policy statement
This Bill seeks to prohibit the public sale and use of fireworks in New Zealand. Under
the Bill, approved public displays will continue to be permitted.
The Bill aims to address the widespread public concern about the adverse effects of
fireworks on animal welfare, public safety, and the environment. Advocacy groups
have raised concerns regarding these risks, and there have been popular public peti‐
tions supporting control.
Fireworks can potentially cause severe distress to livestock, wildlife, and domestic
pets. The sudden loud sounds and flashes of light have a tendency to lead to panic,
injury, and even death. Veterinarians commonly report increased cases of anxiety-
related disease and lost pets following firework events.
Abuse of fireworks have resulted in property damage, personal injury, and an
increased burden on emergency services. Fire hazards, particularly during dry condi‐
tions, pose a serious threat to towns and countryside communities. By restricting pub‐
lic access to fireworks, the Bill aims to reduce these threats and improve community
safety overall.
Clause by clause analysis
Clause 1 is the Title clause.
Clause 2 is the commencement clause and provides for the Bill to come into force the
day after Royal assent.
```
